data.name: Pinball
data.detailed_description: Jogo Pinball 3D com uma incrível nova funcionalidade: um Editor de Mesa para que possa criar e jogar nas suas próprias mesas. Pinball inclui 10 mesas originais e um número crescente de mesas online criadas por jogadores de todo o mundo. Experiencie os vários efeitos incríveis neste original e altamente divertido jogo de Pinball. Com leis físicas realistas, sons divertidos e mesas ilimitadas, Pinball irá mantê-lo agarrado.

reviews.review:
All indications so far are that the developers of PINBALL have spent about as much time on this game (especially since its release) as they did on the name. They failed to provide portrait mode (itself not actually all that uncommon among indie pinball developers) but they included controller input ONLY (and poorly at that, according to player response.) That means that without the option for rebinding keyboard keys, many players can’t play at all, or only with varying degrees of limitation.

Perhaps Pinball’s more serious transgression is to release on a Friday, assuming that numerous copies will be sold before the overused excuse of “Who works on a weekend?” expires on Monday. In other words, there has been ZERO developer response to issues brought forth in Pinball discussion forums. One presumes that developer baKno Games  will offer players their in-game online Support as reason to ignore Steam discussions, but most of what’s online is in the form of FAQ or player forums. And after 15 games, bakNo surely knows what Steam players expect, and that is to have all player issues available to them in one place, not to hide them (or themselves) online.

I said above that the developers of Pinball spent minimal time on “their” game. Well, not only have they ignored their customers thus far, but the entire premise of this game is that the players are supposed to be the ones doing most of the work, by means of a table editor included with the game. (What is offered on the Store Page is 10 baKno tables and “unlimited” player tables, a claim impossible to either measure or validate.) Perhaps this whole concept of “The Invisible Developers” was the entire strategy behind Pinball in order to emphasize the editor (and a strategy with some merit perhaps), but it’s sort of hard to place a lot of faith in a company that has released 14 of 15 Steam games for the same price….exactly $4.99. As in, “Hey! Let’s put a selling price of EXACTLY $4.99 worth of resources into a pinball game!” (Perhaps this "profit wall" is the reason for the lifeless “Custom” settings button.) Or perhaps this entire game serves no other purpose than to gain legal control of the name “Pinball”.

In full honesty, I haven't played any Pinball, but not for lack of desire. I'm one of many players that doesn't CHOOSE to rebind keyboard keys, but instead NEEDs to rebind keyboard keys to be able to play with my one good hand. (In literally thousands of hours of Steam pinball, rebinding to be able to play has never been an issue before.) I’ll wait to refund, but mainly in the event I need to have ownership to continue reviewing. And despite all I’ve said, the reason I purchased on Day One is that I really wanted more pinball. But only if it’s actual pinball, and so far, Pinball isn’t pinball.

Thank you.
